office_does: The assessor values every taxable property in Clallam County each year for property taxes; levy rates are set by taxing districts and voters.
race_blurb: Open seat; current Assessor Pam Rushton is not on the ballot. The office's lead appraiser, Lee Hancock, faces Antonio Price, a diesel mechanic and farmer making his first run for office.

candidates.summary: Lead appraiser in the Clallam County Assessor's Office after 16 years there, with prior careers in mortgage banking and residential contracting.
highlights: 16 years as a residential and commercial appraiser in the assessor's office, now lead appraiser [S1]
13 years in mortgage banking and real estate finance; four years as a self-employed residential contractor [S1]
Running 'to help make the office as efficient as possible' with fair, respectful service [S1]

experience.basis: Runs on 16 years inside the assessor's office as an appraiser and lead appraiser, though he has never held elected office.

candidates.summary: Sequim diesel mechanic, farmer and tow truck driver making his first run for office, who says he wants to help the community.
highlights: First run for office; describes himself as 'a blue-collar' young man who has worked the farmland [S1]
Work experience as a diesel mechanic, farmer and tow truck driver; high school diploma [S1]
Said assessor 'was one thing I felt that I could actually understand and figure out what needs to be done' [S3]

experience.basis: First-time candidate from outside government and the assessment field, running as a community member rather than on professional credentials.
